churn_resistance.rationale: The bones are right — one data module, one config file, no reliance on framework internals — but the home page's logic exists in two parallel implementations, the API layer is untyped any with strict mode off, and the 404/not-found handling is copy-pasted six times. Those are the places where a requirement change or an API shape change will ripple.

findings.issue: The client script re-implements the server-side filter, pagination, URL-building, and humanize() logic from the frontmatter; the two implementations must be edited in lockstep.
findings.suggestion: Extract humanize, the filter predicate, and URL building into src/lib (e.g. filters.ts) and import them in both the frontmatter and the processed <script> — Astro bundles shared modules into client scripts, so one implementation serves both.

findings.issue: The data layer is untyped (api<T = any>, resource: any) and tsconfig sets strict: false, so changes to the PokeAPI shape won't be caught at build time.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the API responses consumed by the app (species, pokemon, move, type, generation) at the boundaries in pokeapi.ts and turn on strict mode; the app already has the right module to centralize them.

findings.issue: export const prerender = false is declared in all 8 page files but is redundant under output: 'server' — the Astro 7 docs explicitly annotate this line 'Not needed in server mode'.
findings.suggestion: Delete the export from the pages; if intent needs documenting, a comment in astro.config.mjs is enough.

findings.issue: 404.astro and [...path].astro are byte-identical; the catch-all route makes the 404 page unreachable, leaving two copies of the same page to maintain.
findings.suggestion: Keep the [...path].astro catch-all and delete 404.astro (or vice versa), since either one alone covers all unmatched URLs under output: 'server'.

findings.issue: The try/catch → isNotFound → set 404 status block is copy-pasted across four [name].astro pages.
findings.suggestion: Add a helper in pokeapi.ts such as fetchOr404(name, endpoint) that returns null on 404, reducing each page to one call.

findings.issue: Inlines a /\/(\d+)\/?$/ regex that duplicates the existing idFromUrl helper from lib/pokeapi.ts.
findings.suggestion: Reuse idFromUrl so the URL-parsing rule lives in exactly one place.

findings.issue: Column sorting parses rendered cell textContent and Number()s it, so any future formatting change (units, % signs, different dash glyph) silently breaks sort order.
findings.suggestion: Emit a data-sort-value attribute on each cell during server rendering and sort on that, falling back to text for string columns.

findings.issue: The default sprite path pattern /media/sprites/pokemon/{id}.png is duplicated in index.astro:27 and PokemonCard.astro:16.
findings.suggestion: Move it into a defaultSpriteUrl(id) helper in pokeapi.ts next to mediaUrl().

findings.issue: Astro 7 stabilized route caching (memoryCache() provider, routeRules, Astro.cache), which would suit this read-heavy app; it re-renders every request instead, relying only on the hand-rolled data cache.
findings.suggestion: Optional, not a defect: consider cache: { provider: memoryCache() } plus a conservative routeRule (e.g. short maxAge on /pokemon/[name]) to reduce per-request rendering cost; the spec permits it since the data cache already keeps responses fresh.

summary: This app is pinned to the current stable Astro (7.4.4, two days old at review time) with only the framework and its Node adapter as dependencies, and every framework and web-platform API in use is verified current — nothing is legacy or deprecated. Data access is cleanly centralized in one typed-any module and configuration lives in one file, so an Astro upgrade would be low-friction. What will age poorly is duplication: the home page's filter logic exists in two parallel implementations, the 404 path is copy-pasted six times, and the untyped data layer means API changes surface as runtime bugs rather than type errors.

apis.replacement: No replacement needed: Astro 7 docs annotate it 'Not needed in server mode' when output is 'server' (docs.astro.build/en/guides/caching)
Unused but available; would be the current-gen way to cache rendered responses on top of the hand-rolled data cache in app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:17
